title: Officeholder
description: A natural person occupying (or having occupied) an elective Office in the United States.

legal_name.description: The Officeholder's legal name as it appears on their filings.

common_name.description: The name the Officeholder is commonly known by, when it differs from legal_name.

party.description: Party affiliation as reported on the most recent filing. Free-text; not interpreted.

offices.description: The Offices this person has held, in the order the register recorded them, the earliest first: a published list only grows at its end (INVARIANTS.md §14). Each Office's term_start and term_end are the seat's term, never the days this person held it; when this person was sworn is sworn_at, and a roster that stopped listing them is a change row in data/changes.ndjson.

sworn_at.description: The day the primary source records this person as sworn into the first Office listed, where it records one. For the House, the sworn-date in the Clerk's roster, which is the swearing-in for the Congress the roster lists, not the start of the person's service: a returning Member carries the new Congress's date. Distinct from the Office's term_start, which is the seat's term. A Signal reads this, never the notes; it does not say whether the person held the office before that date.

biographical_ids.description: External identifiers useful for cross-referencing (never used as sole basis for a Finding).

bioguide_id.description: Biographical Directory of the U.S. Congress ID.

roster_entry_sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the bytes of the Clerk's roster that state this officeholder's seat and member-info, the facts the register reads, found without the XML parser, in the roster the row was read from. A later roster whose entry has the same hash said nothing new about them, so a fact read otherwise from it, or a reading that no longer lists them while the bytes still carry their entry, is the register's own reading, and the build refuses rather than record it as the source's (COUNCIL.md §5, mode 10). A row the register published before the adapter wrote this field gains it from the first later entry that states the facts it carries; that is a later read's entry, whose bytes the register keeps only where a change row cites them, so a later reader may hold the hash and not the bytes. The bytes hashed are the <statedistrict> element followed directly by the <member-info> element, as the roster serves them. The build weighs an entry against the one the register last read for the row (the run record's entries_read), not only this one.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 of the source document, if computable.

examples.notes: Fixture only. Not a real person.
